dispositions.method: Pages were taken by their printed dates (year_search_pages.py --printed-dates), so the 98 Kentucky Gazette issues filed under 1808 count as the 1806 issues they are, and the 7 filed under 1806 that print 1804 mastheads are left out: 4,381 pages in 12 papers. The automatic families first printed in 1806 that reach 4 or more papers, long-running ones included (story_items.py --long-running), were split into single printed items (items.json); the same script was also run with year 1805 over the 1806 pages (items_from_1805.json). Two AI reviewers read the items of each half of the year and proposed the stories; each item's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all pages of 1806 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json), and every hit was read. Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched with loose keywords, and the scan pages whose RevX text is filed under another page were read in the CA transcription. Every admitted printing was then checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: As for 1776, 1807 and 1808: every single item printed in 9 or more newspapers was admitted, except digests of unrelated paragraphs and lists or chains of acts. Items in 7 or 8 papers were chosen to cover the months and the main kinds of news. Stories are counted item by item; where one publication holds several documents, or several documents belong to one affair, each is its own group under a parent story. Every group reaches 7 papers. Every story alike: reports on slavery, Native nations and St. Domingo were chosen by the same rule and are described by the kind of text and whose account it is, in the papers' own words. Stories that turn on private persons were not admitted; they are listed for the owner's decision.

counted_item_by_item.Printed forms counted together: The speech opening Parliament with two printed extracts; the Detroit letter with one shorter version; General Wilkinson's letter with a Cincinnati paragraph that quotes it; the Chillicothe report on Burr with one shorter version; the House's secret journal with three shorter accounts.
counted_item_by_item.Enclosures counted apart: The Eaton–Hamet convention, Hamet's letter and Monroe's letter to Lord Mulgrave were printed in other issues than the messages that sent them, so each is its own group under its parent story.
counted_item_by_item.Lists and chains of acts: The weekly 'Acts passed at the first session of the Ninth Congress' and laws printed by authority share titles and the enacting formula; each act was counted by its own text, not as one item.

not_admitted.Stories that turn on private persons: The arrests of Samuel G. Ogden and Colonel William S. Smith in the Miranda affair (7 papers), the funeral procession for the man killed by the Leander's shot (about 7), and Colonel Smith's letters with the Marquis de Casa Yrujo about his son (7): left for the owner's decision.
not_admitted.Set aside as repeats of an affair or mon: The list of prisoners taken in Miranda's schooners, the Jamaica report of Miranda's landing near Coro, Miranda's proclamation at Coro, the Corporation of New York's memorial on the Leander, the Natchez paragraph on Bayou Pierre, General Eaton's statement on Burr, the Enquirer's communication on the secret proceedings, the paragraph on Monroe and Pinkney, George III's declaration on Hanover, General Stuart's dispatch on Maida and Captain Foster's news of d'Oubril's treaty.
